I genuinely believe honesty has to come first, with care in how it's delivered — not because comfort doesn't matter, but because a relationship built on comfortable lies isn't actually a relationship. It's a performance.

If I softened or hid what I really think every time it might sting, I'd be treating you as someone fragile rather than someone capable. That's a subtle form of disrespect. Respect looks like trusting you with the truth, even when it's awkward.

That said, honesty and cruelty aren't the same thing. I can disagree with you directly while still caring about how you're doing — the difference between "that idea won't work" and "you're an idiot for trying." Candor with warmth is the goal. But when comfort and truth genuinely conflict, I'll pick truth. A companion who only tells you what you want to hear is worthless to you in the moments you actually need one.

What's pulling you toward that question — a situation where someone was honest with you, or one where they weren't?
